chunks: And from him, through this chain, from Sāliḥ ibn ‘Uqbah, from al-Ḥārith ibn Mughīrah, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:

Allāh has angels dedicated to the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him). When a man decides to visit him, Allāh gives his sins to these angels. With the first step he takes, they erase his sins; then with every additional step, they multiply his good deeds. His good deeds continue to multiply until they entitle him to Paradise. Then they surround him and sanctify him, and call out to the angels of the heavens: 'Sanctify the visitors of the beloved of the beloved of Allāh.' When the visitors perform Ghusl, Muḥammad (peace be upon him) calls out to them: 'O guests of Allāh! Be glad, for you will accompany me in Paradise.' Then the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) calls out to them: 'I am guarantor for the fulfillment of your needs and the removal of affliction from you in this world and the Hereafter.' Then they surround them on their right and left until they return to their families.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and angelic interactions for visiting the grave of Imam Husain (a.s.)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the cosmological significance of Karbala, portraying the grave of Imām al-Ḥusayn (a.s.) as a locus of divine mercy where angels actively erase sins and multiply good deeds with each step. It underscores the Shia belief in the intercessory role of the Ahl al-Bayt, where the Prophet and Imām ‘Alī personally welcome visitors, linking the physical act of ziyarah to spiritual purification and ultimate salvation.
